title: Subsets modulo small sets: quotient Boolean algebras

based_on.title: A Course in Universal Algebra
based_on.pages: 127–130 (IV §3, Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.5, and Definition 3.6; Millennium Edition, 2012 update)

summary: Ignoring small differences preserves set operations and turns almost containment into an order on classes.
abstract: Sets that differ only on an allowed small set can be treated as the same object. When the allowed small sets include the empty set and stay small under taking subsets and finite unions, union, intersection, and complement still give consistent operations on these objects. For subsets of the natural numbers modulo finite sets, finite sets become zero and nonzero objects represent infinite sets; containment means containment with finitely many exceptions. Each nonzero object splits into two nonzero disjoint pieces. Assuming choice, every countable descending sequence of nonzero objects has a nonzero object below them all.
